title: Use cases and domain entities
idea: Requirement analysis turns a vague brief into use cases (who does what, under which rule) and entities (the things those rules are about), before any class is coded.
points: A use case is an actor's goal plus its rule: 'only the owner cancels'.
Nouns in the use cases suggest entities; verbs become methods on a service.
Entities have identity and refer to each other by id, never by copied fields.
In interviews, read use cases back and ask what is out before drawing classes.

code.title: The problem
code.caption: A model copied from a screen layout stores a snapshot of the email. When HR fixes it, reminders go stale.

walk.text: `BookingRow` mirrors the booking screen: room, email, times. It looks complete to a UI designer.
The factory reads the email once and drops the employee id. The link to the person is gone.
HR corrects the address in the one place that owns it, the directory.
Both reminders still use the old address, while the directory holds the new one.
Without an employee id the rule 'only the owner may cancel' cannot even be checked.

code.title: The fix
code.caption: Entities from the use cases, linked by id, each guarding its own invariants at construction.

walk.text: `Building` and `Room` come from the facilities use case. A room with no seats is rejected.
`Employee` owns the email. It is the single source of truth for contact details.
`Booking` stores `roomId` and `employeeId`, not copies. The slot must sit inside 0 to 24.
`isOwnedBy` answers the cancel rule directly from the stored id.
After HR's change, the reminder resolves the id and gets the current address.
Invalid rooms and slots fail fast with messages that name the bad value.

pitfalls: Modelling from screens copies fields into bookings; data drifts when the source changes.
Skipping the actor column hides rules like 'only the owner cancels' until code review.
Turning every noun into a class: 'slot' and 'calendar' are values or queries here, not entities.

quiz.q: In CopiedFieldsBug, what does the reminder line for B2 print?
quiz.why: `BookingRow.of` copied the email when B2 was created. Updating the directory later does not touch the copy, so the stale address prints.

takeaway: Use cases give the rules; entities hold identity and link by id.
